scope: art-side customiser data proposal (Snapchat/Bitmoji-style); NOT the backend Look schema

look.base: manifest base id (fixes gender, family, skeleton proportions)
look.skin: skin_01..skin_10 from this export skin_palette (fair -> deep); UI ids collide with older hexes: translate explicitly
look.parts: {head, top, bottom, feet}: keys from the base family library (modular families only); omitted = base default
look.hair: UBC only: hair_library key or none; modular families pick hair via parts.head
look.facial: UBC m only: additive facial hair list
look.tints: {skin, hair, top, bottom, shoes, accent, hat, brows}: palette names or #hex; brows default = brow_color(hair)
look.accessories: list of base accessory keys; one per socket; flags hides_hair/occludes_face/emissive

validation: reject parts from another family or a non-modular base
reject bottom/feet and top/bottom pairs listed as gaps
reject two accessories on one socket
sum the selected tier of every visible part + accessories and gate on budgets.triangles
resolve completely or refuse: never keep a stale default actor when a part is missing
tint_formula: sequential per region: out = lerp(out, tint * min(luminance(out) / max(0.03, luminance(tint_reference[region])), 1.6), mask); luminance in linear light; masks non-colour; family atlases store tintable texels as shade x #9a9a9a so every part of a family re-colours identically
tint_resolution: modular families: tints = default_tints of the selected parts (feet, bottom, top, head order) <- base look_defaults <- user tints; brows = brow_color(final hair) unless the user sets brows. UBC/heroes: base look_defaults <- user tints.
